attempts.raw_response: The position was critical. The new Governor, Mr. Drake, had fled, and the few Europeans who remained were hard pressed to hold the factory against overwhelming numbers. It was at this juncture that Mr. Holwell, afterwards so famous for his suffering in the Black Hole, took command of the defence. The odds were desperate—some five hundred Europeans and sepoys against an army of fifteen thousand men under Siraj-ud-daula's walls. Yet they held out for three days, hoping for relief from the ships in the river. When none came, and the magazine was about to blow, surrender became inevitable. The terms granted were generous: personal property was to be respected, and the garrison was to be allowed to march out with honours of war. It was a creditable defence, and one which reflected great credit upon the small band who made it.
